$comment: Provenance manifest for zone GeoJSON layers. Update fetched_on, vintage, and caveats each time a layer is refreshed. Generated 2026-05-21 from audit-2026-05-21-*.md. Zone layer refresh (roadmap items 1 and 7) applied 2026-07-02.

layers.label: TIF Districts
layers.sourceAgency: City of Chicago — Department of Planning and Development
layers.caveats: 100 active TIF districts as of portal refresh 2026-01-27 (dataset eejr-xtfb). The 9 districts that expired 12/31/2025 have already been removed from the portal's active dataset and are not in this file. 13 more expire 12/31/2026. The Civic Federation's '124 active' count (2025) was likely measured before the Dec 2025 expirations. Properties refreshed: TIF_Number, District_Name, IND, Type, Use, SBIF, Community_Areas, Wards, Approval_Date, Expiration_Date, Status. Previous dataset ID dchz-72ji is no longer active on the portal.

layers.label: Special Service Areas
layers.caveats: 58 features; matches current citywide SSA count.

layers.label: Illinois Enterprise Zones
layers.sourceAgency: Illinois DCEO + City of Chicago EZ Administrator
layers.caveats: 6 polygons (Chicago EZ I-VI). All expire 2030; recertification window opens 2028.

layers.label: Federal Opportunity Zones
layers.sourceAgency: U.S. Department of the Treasury / IRS
layers.caveats: 181 features. Valid through 12/31/2028. OBBBA (July 2025) made OZ permanent on decennial cycle; OZ 2.0 tracts certified by Treasury late 2026, effective 1/1/2027 — refresh required then.

layers.label: Illinois Opportunity Zones
layers.caveats: 24 features in current file — appears to be a Chicago subset, not the full ~327 IL OZ tracts. Verify scope. Illinois must nominate ~238 new tracts in H2 2026 effective 1/1/2027.

layers.label: HUD Qualified Census Tracts
layers.sourceAgency: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
layers.caveats: 370 Cook County QCTs for 2026 (down from 418 in 2024 baseline; 62 tracts dropped, 14 added). 246 Chicago city tracts + 124 suburban Cook County tracts. Source: HUD ArcGIS service QUALIFIED_CENSUS_TRACTS_2026 (filter STATE=17 AND COUNTY=031). Refresh annually each January 1 when HUD publishes new designations.

layers.label: NMTC Eligible Census Tracts
layers.caveats: 695 features. Re-baselines with each 5-year ACS release. Refresh when 2019-2023 ACS NMTC eligibility lookup is published by CDFI Fund (expected mid-2026). Program made permanent by OBBBA (July 2025).

layers.label: State Incentive Zones (EDGE / REV / MICRO / Data Center proxy)
layers.caveats: Proxy boundary — REV / EDGE / MICRO / Data Center programs are project-by-project, not zone-based. The 114-feature high-unemployment census-tract overlay is used as an approximation for the 'underserved area' enhanced-credit eligibility. Same file is referenced by edge-zones, rev-zones, micro-zones, data-center-zones. See edge-zones-official.geojson for the official DCEO underserved area tract layer (739 Cook County tracts).

layers.label: Chicago Landmark Districts
layers.sourceAgency: City of Chicago — Commission on Chicago Landmarks (DPD-HP)
layers.caveats: 59 features. District names refreshed to match authoritative portal names (data.cityofchicago.org/d/zidz-sdfj). Geometries unchanged; originally sourced from State Plane and reprojected to WGS84 in Feb 2026. The portal's Landmark Districts dataset (zidz-sdfj) has not been updated since 2009 and contains 59 features — the same as our file. The 2025 Landmarks Ordinance PDF cites 62 districts; the 3 additional designations (post-2009) do not appear in any publicly downloadable geospatial dataset and cannot be confirmed or geolocated from official sources. Boundaries for those 3 districts were not added to this file. Next refresh: monitor data.cityofchicago.org/d/zidz-sdfj and the Commission on Chicago Landmarks announcements for updated spatial data.

layers.label: DCEO Underserved Areas — Official (EDGE / REV / MICRO / Data Center / Apprenticeship)
layers.geometrySource: U.S. Census Bureau TIGER/Web 2024 (tigerWMS_Current, layer 8, Census Tracts)
layers.scope: Cook County — all underserved tracts per DCEO 2026 designation
layers.vintage: 2022-2026 DCEO designation (expires end of calendar year 2026)
layers.caveats: 739 Cook County census tracts designated underserved by DCEO for 2026. Joined from DCEO's official Excel spreadsheet (Underserved Census Tracts 2022-2026.xlsx) to Census TIGER 2024 tract geometries. The designation covers tracts meeting at least one of four statutory criteria: (1) poverty rate >= 20%; (2) >= 35% families with children below 130% poverty; (3) >= 20% households receiving SNAP; (4) unemployment >= 120% of national average for 2 consecutive years. The existing edge-zones.geojson proxy (114 features, high-unemployment only) is left in place untouched. This file replaces the proxy for any address lookup requiring official EDGE/REV/MICRO/Data Center/Apprenticeship underserved-area enhanced-credit eligibility. IMPORTANT: The 2022-2026 designation expires at end of 2026; monitor DCEO for the 2027+ list.

layers.label: Triple-Benefit Zones (informational)
